scenes.line1: How do you keep goroutines safe?
scenes.say: Go makes concurrency easy, but how do you keep goroutines from stepping on each other? Which tool should you use for safe access?

scenes.label: Mutex
scenes.sub: Locks code so only one goroutine runs it.
scenes.say: Use a mutex to lock critical sections. Only one goroutine can enter at a time.
WaitGroup lets you wait for goroutines to finish. Once ensures a function runs just one time. Atomic handles simple updates without locks.

scenes.code:
var mu sync.Mutex
mu.Lock()
// critical section
mu.Unlock()
scenes.say: Here's a mutex in action. Lock before the critical section, unlock after.

scenes.question: How do you avoid deadlocks with Mutex?
scenes.right: Always lock and unlock in the same order. Use defer mu.Unlock() right after locking.
scenes.say: A common trap is deadlocks with mutexes. Always lock and unlock in the same order, and use defer to guarantee unlock.
